Retailo · B2B ordering, 2020–2021 · Earlier work

Helping Karachi’s shopkeepers restock on their own, cutting support time from 80 minutes to under 9

six-month consulting role

Team

Summary

Retailo let neighbourhood shopkeepers restock from their phones, with thousands of products and next-day delivery. It was the first app of its kind in Pakistan, backed by one of the country’s largest seed rounds.

Retailers loved the prices, but they kept going back to their distributors, even paying more. Many of the orders that did come in were placed by phone, through our own activation team, and the call centre couldn’t keep up.

I took design, product and engineering into shops across Karachi, and we rebuilt the app around how retailers actually shop: by picture, in their own language, with help on WhatsApp.

<9 minto resolve a support request, down from 80
+62%retention among retailers ordering on their own
+36%orders scheduled for a later date

Where it started

The prices were working; the app wasn’t. Two things kept retailers from ordering on their own.

  1. The old way was easier. Distributors came to the shop. Retailers knew them, and paid a premium for that comfort.
  2. Orders depended on people. Early on, the activation team placed orders by phone on retailers’ behalf. As Retailo grew, the call centre buckled, orders were missed, and customers left angry. The practice survived because it was still the easiest way to order.

How might we help retailers order and restock without customer support stepping in?

What we saw in the field

We ran shadow visits to align everyone on the same problem. Product designers, product managers, engineers and creatives took turns visiting retailers in the remotest parts of Karachi, as far out as Orangi Town.

On one visit, a shopkeeper asked me whether the app was only for educated people. That question set the brief.

  1. They navigated by picture. Most couldn’t read English script, and many couldn’t read Urdu either.
  2. Reading wrong meant ordering wrong. Guessing from text, retailers ordered the wrong sizes and the wrong pack counts.
  3. When unsure, they called. Every hesitation became a phone call, and every phone call leaned on our team.

Tested the same day

After each visit, I sat down with our designers and engineers to sketch fixes we could build quickly and that would hold up with everyone, including our hands-on investors in Saudi Arabia. Paper wireframes went to shops nearby the same day.

Then came the big one: more than fifteen guerrilla usability sessions at Retailo’s monthly retailers’ convention, with retailers and delivery drivers alike.

Three decisions

Each one took a reason to call and designed it out of the app.

Pictures first, words second

Every category and product leads with a large photo of what’s actually on the shelf, and prices read as numbers. In testing, this let retailers tell at a glance whether a listing was a single item or a pack, which brand it was, and whether it was genuine.

What we gave upDensity. Photos take room, so retailers scroll more. We chose recognition over fitting more on a screen.

Sign in in your own language

Language comes first, before the phone number. Retailers pick English, Urdu, Arabic or Roman Urdu, their own language in English script, and the app follows. Feedback from across Pakistan, and from bakala owners in the Gulf as Retailo moved into Saudi Arabia, put this at the start of onboarding.

Help where they already are

Whether they were in Karachi or Dammam, retailers already lived on WhatsApp. Customer support agreed, so we put a WhatsApp button in every header, and a help screen with two ways out: call us, or chat. Questions that used to queue for the call centre were now answered in a chat.

Support resolution fell from 80 minutes to under 9.

Results

The app stopped depending on the call centre. Retailers ordered on their own, came back, and started planning ahead.

  • Under 9 minutes to resolve a support request, down from 80
  • +62% retention among retailers ordering on their own, with no manual order taking
  • +36% orders scheduled for a later date

What I took from it

Retailo is where I learned to design for people who are rarely designed for. Pictures before words, the person’s own language, and help in the app they already use. I have carried all three since, most recently into Careem’s sign-up for markets with recycled SIM cards and low trust.
